role: exploratory: is the training-data threshold found on banking (section 3.23) the same on the other two domains?
claim: On the banking workflow the hosted model alone is the better choice below about 5 labelled examples per intent, the hybrid from about 6, and the specialist alone matches the best zero-shot hosted model from about 12. This protocol repeats the sweep on MASSIVE and CLINC150 with the same rules and joins each specialist to the saved zero-shot answers of the hosted models on that domain's sessions (sections 3.26 and 3.27). No API call. Written before any model in this file was trained.
subsample: per label, a random max(1, round(fraction x count)) of that label's training rows, seed 20261012

recipes.encoder: the Program 2 encoder recipe at learning rate 1e-4, log loss; 3 epochs or as many as give at least 300 optimizer steps
recipes.massive_decoder: the primary protocol's decoder recipe unchanged (2e-5), with the same epoch rule
recipes.clinc_decoder: not run: 150 options make each decoder step about twice as slow as on Banking77
recipes.full_data_rows: MASSIVE: the size sweep's 150M encoder at 1e-4 and the primary decoder. CLINC150: the threshold encoder of section 3.27.

scope: a threshold on the top probability, chosen on dev by the workflow v1 rule, for every specialist. On MASSIVE this rule is known to work badly (section 3.26); that is part of what is being measured.
join: each specialist alone, and first with its least confident 10, 25, 40 and 60 percent of turns sent to each hosted model; each hosted model alone
readout: per domain, the smallest training size at which the specialist alone matches the best zero-shot hosted model alone, and the smallest at which the best hybrid does
limits: One seed per fraction. Hosted models zero-shot. CLINC150 has exactly 100 training rows per intent, so 1% is one example per intent; MASSIVE is imbalanced, so a fraction is not a fixed number per intent.
